| | | | Peter, How do you successfully execute a 45-million-acre corporate land grab? **Step one:** You take an executive who spent his career lobbying to chop down national forests. **Step two:** You appoint him as the Chief of the U.S. Forest Service. Step three: You wait for him to open the floodgates. **That is exactly what is happening right now in Washington.** Tom Schultz is the first-ever Forest Service Chief who didn't actually come from within the agency. Before this, he was the president of a timber trade association. Now, he is using his government authority to completely kill the 25-year-old "roadless rule," stripping protections from 45 million acres of untouched wilderness so his former employers can bulldoze roads and clear-cut the backcountry. The politicians rubber-stamping this heist are looking the American public in the eye and claiming they need to build logging roads into pristine habitats to "prevent wildfires." It is complete garbage. [**This is a 45-million-acre heist happening in broad daylight. Will you pitch in $10 today to our rapid-response war chest so we can expose this corruption?**](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/cJ4ZhxvfEZrbcpTG1pYzbg~~/AAUS1hA~/gICB6g64aUMg0K33LisJOS4ry3dMuYJ7vCwM1PIzerk4-L7-QoFlTMnLwSigFhxxIW0HcUDLjbZ3WTt4DzSohRJ5Q6aPxXelEnsQWaPR1SCYCVNH72Hqr1KcO1T8t0-yAP6nf1z0U2C1V_XLoOYjaOxmoOF2AHR1m77n89-G8kP8BpGf7dBA8WSkbF11ml4l6RqLPLhaoutTGEkZPphMR6uxP4Oc-MDW1K8IuqHdawZC69CJ9ZgB_hKEvK0d6aOT) The Forest Service's _own data_ shows that wildfires are nearly three times as likely to start near roads because they bring in human ignition sources. They aren't trying to stop forest fires—they are using the threat of fires as a human shield for the timber lobby. And the lumber executives know it. They are literally bragging on corporate earnings calls, telling their Wall Street investors, "We know the new Forest Service chief." Schultz and the politicians enabling him think they can quietly liquidate the last remaining old-growth forests in America without facing any consequences. They expect you to be too exhausted by the news cycle to put up a fight. We are going to ensure that every hunter, angler, hiker, and voter knows exactly who allowed a timber lobbyist to sell off our national heritage. Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth broke barriers in 2024, becoming the youngest woman ever elected to Congress from Maryland. She went to Congress with one thing in mind: delivering for Maryland families on the issues that matter most. Whether it's standing up for federal workers, supporting veterans, protecting the Chesapeake Bay, or tackling the affordability crisis head-on, Sarah is on the front lines, fighting for what is right. And Sarah has delivered on her promises. She has spent her first year in the House advocating for the Third District, successfully passing five bills into law, solving over 1,000 constituent cases, and bringing tens of millions in funding back to her community. She learned her work ethic and tenacity from growing up in a union household and honed her skills of problem-solving and collaborating over six years in the Maryland State Senate. Sarah lives in Annapolis with her husband, Eric, and their dog, Ollie. The cameras were still packing up. As soon as President Trump finished taking questions from a hostile press corps in the Rose Garden, one of his top aides walked straight up to him and handed him a clean, professional binder.**President Trump didn’t smile for the cameras. He opened the binder and started reviewing it immediately.** ******

body:
The New York Times last polled our race 3 months ago and found us down 7. This poll has swung 10 points since then.

| | |
---
Friend, look at this:
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5897?refcode=jtk1548-bu-nd&t=1&akid=13086%2E400544%2EWbtw2C)
In June, _The_ _New York Times_ /Siena poll had me trailing Greg Abbott by 7 points, 51% to 44%.
**Now, that same poll has me ahead, 49% to 46%.**
That's a 10-point swing in three months, from one of the most respected pollsters in the country. It's not a fluke, either. | | | |

Friend,

We've looked at the polling in every swing state and swing race in the country. It's margin of error, either way, almost everywhere.

At this point, it's not about winning anybody over. _It's about who actually shows up._

If conservatives turn out in November, we'll win every critical battleground and lay the groundwork for victory in 2028 and beyond.

That's why Turning Point Action is focusing all our efforts on three key states: Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire.

**We call these states the new RED WALL.**

After 2024, Charlie looked at the numbers, looked at the maps, and told our team something simple. If we lock down Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire, the Left's entire strategy falls apart. Their map collapses. Their path back to power disappears.

Here's why... Winning the presidency comes down to 270 electoral votes. Lose Arizona and most of the realistic paths to the White House in 2028 are gone. Lose Nevada and New Hampshire and the Left rebuilds the Blue Wall they lost in 2024.

Whoever wins in 2028 controls the 2030 Census. The Census drives redistricting. Redistricting sets the congressional map for the next ten years.

This midterm decides which way that goes.

Jim Himes is polished, articulate, and comfortable in front of a television camera. He's good at it like an actor and could be nominated for an Oscar for his performances and sound bites criticizing President Trump, and exaggerating his impact in representing the people of Connecticut.
But Congress isn't Hollywood and the Congress Street Bridge in Bridgeport that he ran on fixing 18 years ago has become a park and a homeless encampment.
Congress is where laws are written, taxpayer dollars are spent, and decisions are made that affect our families, businesses, and communities.
**The question isn 't how good Jim Himes looks on television. It's what he's actually doing for Connecticut and as the saying goes - "Is he bringing home the bacon?" If I shook a Magic 8 ball the Survey says No.**
## So What Does the Record Show?
The website [YourRepRecord](https://substack.com/redirect/7a29eba6-e52e-494f-a770-c32e10e89051?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) tracks congressional voting activity across 12 policy areas.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/22edeb2e-81ce-46f0-af2d-c73589f658d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Its October 9, 2026 report contains 162 entries for Congressman Himes during the 119th Congress.
## The Issues That Affect Connecticut Families
Here is the website's complete issue-by-issue scorecard:
**Healthcare -- What about affordability? - Jim Scores a C**
Himes supports extending Affordable Care Act subsidies. But what about Medicare Advantage oversight, prescription costs, and expanding benefits for seniors? Families need measurable relief from healthcare expenses.
**Housing and Affordability -- Who pays for the infrastructure? - Jim Scores a C**
Himes supports federal housing incentives. Yet increased development requires roads, sewer capacity, water systems, schools, and other public infrastructure.
Where is Washington's investment in the infrastructure that our communities actually need?
**Immigration -- What happened to enforcement? - Jim does get an A**
Yet, Himes voted against the Laken Riley Act and the SAVE Act. He supports a pathway to citizenship for qualifying DREAMers and Temporary Protected Status holders.
These legislative choices deserve public examination, including their implications for immigration enforcement and election administration.
Jim wants all illegals to become citizens to become future voters.
**Energy -- What about our electric bills? Jim gets an A- on climate not affordable energy**
Himes supports clean-energy incentives and environmental regulations.
But Connecticut households face substantial electricity and heating expenses. What is his plan for expanding reliable generation, improving natural-gas access, and addressing energy affordability?
**Justice and Civil Liberties -- What about constitutional protections? Jim gets a C-**
Himes supported reauthorizing Section 702 of FISA without certain additional warrant protections sought by privacy advocates.
National security matters. So do constitutional liberties. His position deserves scrutiny as this is what our Constitution and our Bill of Rights is all about. Jim's record speaks otherwise.
**Labor - Jim Gets a C+**
His party is no longer the party of the working class.
**Israel -- Jim Gets a C**
Himes has supported maintaining American military assistance to Israel while also supporting humanitarian measures in Gaza and opposing certain sanctions involving the International Criminal Court.
**War & Foreign Policy** \- **Jim Gets a B**
Basically an adequate score.
## And What About Bringing Federal Dollars Back to Connecticut?
After nearly 18 years in Congress, constituents have every reason to ask:
* Where is the federal investment needed for southwestern Connecticut's aging sewer infrastructure?
* What measurable progress has Washington delivered on I-95 congestion?
* How is federal policy helping residents facing high healthcare and energy expenses?
* How much federal funding is returning to our towns to relieve the burden on local taxpayers?

**These are the questions that matter when the television cameras turn off. Also, How Does Jim compare to the rest of Congressional Team from Connecticut? - He ranks 4 out of 5. Yet Courtney has at least brought Jobs to CT with Electric Boat. Himes couldn 't keep the Post Office sorting facility in Stamford.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/da8fea22-ae91-40a2-beae-6b4b3e702c32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
## Congress Is Not a Television Studio
Jim Himes has spent years explaining Washington to Connecticut.
It is equally important that he explain what Washington has delivered for Connecticut, especially in his district.
A congressional representative should be evaluated on legislative actions, funding secured, constituent service, and measurable policy results.
Television appearances tell us what a politician says.
**Congressional records tell us what a politician does.**
And Connecticut residents deserve to examine both.
In a state which is totally controlled and mismanaged by the Democrats being the second worst congressman in Connecticut is not what Connecticut's 4th Congressional District should be sending to Congress.
Where it counts, Himes is not on the side of the people. He fails in healthcare, housing and affordability, he is not pro labor, does not support justice and civil liberty, does not support democracy and voting rights does not support voter ID, likes money influencing politics and is not a supporter of Israel's right to defend itself.
Jim puts on a great act pretending to be for the people, but where it counts he does vote in the best interests of the people of Connecticut. Let's send him to Hollywood but not back to Congress.

It is time for change and to send a Doctor to Congress.

body:

Then immigration agents detain you, and you aren't even allowed to ask a judge to let you go home while your case plays out. Then immigration agents detain you, and you aren't even allowed to ask a judge to let you go home while your case plays out. That's the policy the Supreme Court just agreed to review.1 Mass deportation doesn't only impact immigrants. When a coworker is locked away, the work falls on everyone else. When a neighbor disappears, families lose paychecks and kids lose a parent at the dinner table. Working families already pay $2,358 a year for mass deportation. Citizenship would mean a $4,300 raise.2 The National Association of Home Builders is sounding the alarm. It says this policy has removed workers from the labor force, forced project cancellations, and eliminated jobs for U.S.-born workers, all during a housing shortage.3 Lower courts have overwhelmingly ruled against the administration's policy. A decision is expected by July.1 We'll be watching, and ready to mobilize, whatever the outcome. I told them I will work to cut down on red tape and make sure our rural communities can really thrive. I believe a representative's most important responsibility is to listen to the people they serve and fight for the issues that matter to them. clean_body: The Brewers’ success is not the only kind we need this fall | | | | We aren’t sure about the rest of you, but here at Battleground Wisconsin, we cannot get enough of winning. (We don’t need to talk about the Packers.) With over 100 wins this season, the Milwaukee Brewers are sitting at the TOP of the National League, and they’ve had one of the most exciting series in the playoffs. But, Derek, we never would have experienced this without the work of David Crowley. You heard that right: the Brewers were on the verge of leaving Milwaukee, but David was key in the negotiations to keep the team in downtown Milwaukee for decades to come. Imagine if we were never able to see a Padres home run stopped by the roof??? That’s not a reality we want to live in. Derek, the Brewers’ success is not the only kind we need this fall. There are only 24 days left until the election, and David Crowley is statistically almost tied with far-right MAGA puppet Tom Tiffany. On Friday, in a federal courtroom in Anniston, U.S. District Judge Corey Maze sentenced 28-year-old Eladio Pascual-Gaspar to 31 months in prison for illegal reentry. On any docket, that is a routine case. In his file, it's the last page of a story Washington wrote eleven years earlier.
Here is the arc. In 2015, Pascual-Gaspar crossed the border as an unaccompanied minor. The government handed him to a sponsor and turned him loose -- and, in any sense that matters, stopped watching. In 2021, he pleaded guilty in Mississippi to aiding and abetting an armed robbery. The robbery earned him punishment. The immigration file earned him a deportation, in 2023. Then he walked right back in.
June 2026, Talladega. Police find a 15-year-old -- himself, per court records, in the country illegally -- alone in a car registered to a man named Henry Vegas Mondragon. The car gets towed. A fellow shows up at the lot to claim it, flashing Guatemalan ID under that same made-up name. The ID is fake. So is the name. It is Pascual-Gaspar. Homeland Security Investigations and the Talladega County Drug Task Force built the case; the Justice Department prosecuted it under its Operation Take Back America banner. Friday, Maze made it official: 31 months.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/12a58715-6b94-4c4c-a02a-27d6aeac9fb0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Now study the thing, because one man is one data point with a pipeline behind it.
From fiscal 2015 through 2024, the Office of Refugee Resettlement released nearly 700,000 unaccompanied children to sponsors -- almost 28,000 the year Pascual-Gaspar arrived. In FY2024, 89 percent of discharges went to family sponsors, per the Congressional Research Service. The handoff to the sponsor is where the government's attention ends. Not declines. Ends.
You don't have to take my word for it. DHS's own Inspector General found that ICE cannot effectively monitor the location or status of children after release: roughly 31,000 kids released from 2019 to 2023 had missing or incomplete addresses in their files; as of January 2025, about 233,000 had never been served with a notice to appear in immigration court; another 43,000 were served and simply skipped. That is not a border problem. That is a back-office problem -- and it manufactures reentrants by the boatload.
Which brings me to the part people keep missing: this happened in Alabama.
Alabama is one of the reddest states in the union, and in 2011 it passed HB 56, among the most aggressive state immigration laws ever written. Talladega County is not a sanctuary jurisdiction; it is a drug-task-force jurisdiction. Yet none of that state-level toughness mattered, because the pipeline is federal. Washington releases the minor, loses the file, skips the hearing, waits for the robbery, delegates the deportation, then acts surprised at the reentry. A state can pass any law it likes. It cannot opt out of a federal release program. Talladega didn't fail here. The system upstream did -- and the bill landed on an Alabama tow lot, in an Alabama courtroom, with an Alabama 15-year-old sitting in a car registered to an alias.
Credit where due, because Friday proves something else: the back end worked. A federal judge imposed real prison. Section 1326 means the next return carries enhanced felony time. HSI and the local task force caught him -- but only because he got greedy and walked into a tow lot to reclaim a car he'd registered under his fake name. Luck did the rest. A functioning system shouldn't need that luck.
Three fixes would matter more than another press conference. Vet sponsors and follow up on them -- the Inspector General's own recommendation. Serve the paperwork, because 233,000 kids with no notice to appear are the reentrants of 2030. And stop treating reentry after deportation like a paperwork offense. It is a felony, and this man proved the point by treating his own deportation as a suggestion.
There's a smaller tragedy folded inside this one. The kid in the car is fifteen. Eleven years ago, the kid in the pipeline was one too. Same release, same sponsor handoff, same lost file -- the conveyor belt doesn't just deliver men back to us; it recruits the next lap from the current one.
They released him as a kid. They ignored the armed robbery. They deported him once. He came back with a fake name and another teenager in the car. Stop calling that compassion. It is a conveyor belt, and Americans are paying for every lap.
Sources: DOJ, U.S. Attorney's Office N.D. Ala., press release, Sept. 25, 2026; Anniston Star; WBRC Fox 6; 1819 News; CRS Report R43599; ORR release data (FY2015-24) via National Immigration Forum; DHS Office of Inspector General findings on UAC post-release monitoring.

[ stdin# ]Josh Shapiro for Pennsylvania
Derek, while
you're reading this, there are volunteers knocking doors across
Pennsylvania at this very moment.

Saturday is the biggest voter contact day of our week, every week — and
after today, there are only three of them left before Election Day.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/16567?t=1001&akid=586%2E245147%2Er-TI7m ]Each volunteer we can't fully staff and supply is thousands of
conversations that never happen. So Derek,
will you chip in $10 today and help us
make all three weekends we have left count?

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/16567?t=1002&akid=586%2E245147%2Er-TI7m ]Chip in →

Here's what today looks like on the ground.

Organizers were at staging locations before 9AM this morning, handing out
packets and literature. Volunteers who gave up their own Saturday are
working neighborhoods in every corner of the state. Most of them will
knock on doors until dark, come back tomorrow, and do it again.

That's the part Mar-a-Lago money can't replicate,
Derek. Our far-right opponent
can run all the attack ads she wants, but she can’t buy a few thousand
Pennsylvanians who'd rather spend Saturday knocking doors and having one
conversation at a time because they believe in the work we’re doing.

But Derek,
being able to continue this work — having
every organizer on a payroll, getting every piece of literature printed,
and traveling to every county in Pennsylvania costs money.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/16567?t=1003&akid=586%2E245147%2Er-TI7m ]So Derek, if
you care about the future of our democracy, please chip in
$10
today to help us make the most of these last three Saturdays we get and

must-win race.

name: Craig at Swing Left
subject: We just added 8 new races to our target list
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Swing Left, [swingleft
body:
I wanted to make sure you saw our announcement from earlier this week.
#
Hi there, Craig here, Political Director at Swing Left.
I wanted to make sure you saw our announcement from earlier this week.
With less than a month to go until Election Day, we’ve been closely monitoring swing districts and state races across the country. Based on what we’ve been seeing—changes in the races, an all-time low on Trump’s approval rating, and more—**we made the decision to add 6 more U.S. House races and 2 more governor’s races to our list of targets for this November:**
We’re in a sprint to the finish in these final few weeks, and Democrats have the opportunity to win big across the country—but only if they have the resources to get voters to the polls.
If you’d like to help, you can [**click here to donate to our Flip the House Fund**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/2628?t=1&akid=3094%2E1562180%2E3WeVz6) or [**click here to donate to our Win In The States Fund**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/2629?t=2&akid=3094%2E1562180%2E3WeVz6) today.
Make sure to read below for more information about why we’re adding these specific races. And thank you, as always, for everything you’re doing to build long-term power for Democrats.
Craig
Political Director, Swing Left
\-------- Forwarded message --------
From: Swing Left
Subject: Our final map expansion before Election Day!
Hi there,
As we enter the last four weeks of the election, [Democrats are positioned to do well](https://act.swingleft.org/go/2432?t=3&akid=3094%2E1562180%2E3WeVz6) on Election Day. But the fact remains that Republicans have an outside spending money advantage, and they’re using it to reserve millions of dollars of ad space to attack Democrats and distract from their unpopular agenda and the Trump administration’s blatant corruption.
That makes these final weeks especially important. That’s when many voters will start paying attention to races and when campaigns will make their final push to reach voters.
The Swing Left political team has been closely tracking campaigns across the country, looking at polling, voting trends, fundraising, and what we’re seeing on the ground. Based on that analysis, we believe several additional House and Governor’s races could benefit from an investment now.
As a result, **we’re expanding our Must-Win target list to include 6 more U.S. House races and 2 more Governor’s races!**
Here are all the new races we’re adding to our map:
* **New Hampshire’s 1st Congressional District, Democrat Stefany Shaheen (Must-Hold):** After a competitive primary, Shaheen now faces a wealthy opponent who can self-fund his campaign in this historically swingy district. We need to make sure she has the resources and support needed to overcome her opponent’s money.

* **California's 6th Congressional District, Democrat Dr. Richard Pan (Must-Flip):** Dr. Pan is running against Republican-turned-independent Rep. Kevin Kiley in this newly drawn district. The district was redrawn under Proposition 50 to create a stronger opportunity for Democrats, but Kiley is well-funded and mounting a serious campaign to take this seat.

* **Florida’s 13th Congressional District, Democrat Leela Gray (Must-Flip):** Gray is challenging controversial Republican Rep. Anna Paulina Luna in this light red district. Polls show a tight contest, but Gray entered the race late and needs to catch up on fundraising.

* **Florida’s 22nd Congressional District, Democrat Pia Dandiya (Must-Flip):** Republicans redrew this district earlier this year to lean red, but Democrats still have a path to compete. If the 2020 presidential results were applied to the new district lines, President Biden would have won the district by 3%. In this political environment, Dandiya is running a strong campaign to hold on to this seat and overcome the Republican gerrymander.

* **Kentucky’s 6th Congressional District, Democrat Zach Dembo (Must-Flip):** This open seat leans red, but Democratic Governor Andy Beshear carried it by double digits in his 2023 reelection campaign. Dembo, a former military prosecutor and policy advisor to Gov. Beshear, is running against a vulnerable Republican former state legislator who only moved back to Kentucky to run here.

* **Montana’s 1st Congressional District, Democrat Sam Forstag (Must-Flip):** Former smokejumper Sam Forstag is running against right-wing radio host Aaron Flint for this open seat in western Montana that voted for former Democratic Senator Jon Tester. After winning the Democratic primary with an impressive ground game, Forstag is well-positioned to flip this seat.

[**If you’d like to support Swing Left and the Democratic nominees in all of our most critical red-to-blue House races across the country, click here to make a donation to the Flip the House Fund.**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/2628?t=4&akid=3094%2E1562180%2E3WeVz6)
* **Alaska Governors’ Race, Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins (Must-Flip):** Independent analysts at _Cook Political Report_ just moved this race to “Toss Up” as Democrats have consolidated behind former State Rep. Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, who is facing three conservative Republican candidates. Alaska’s ranked-choice voting means Republicans must ensure that voters rank the other Republican candidates as their second and third choice in order to consolidate the Republican vote–also known as their “rank the red” strategy. That creates an opening for Kreiss-Tomkins to consolidate Democrats, independents, and even moderate Republicans.

* **Texas Governors’ Race, Democrat Gina Hinojosa (Must-Flip):** Polling has shown an increasingly competitive race between state Rep. Gina Hinojosa and 11-year Republican incumbent Governor Greg Abbott. As Trump and GOP Senate nominee Ken Paxton drag down Republicans in Texas, Abbott faces a tough political environment and backlash over positions on issues like data centers. His enormous cash advantage in this expensive state means Hinojosa needs immediate support to stay competitive.

[**You can support Hinojosa and Kreiss-Tomkins by making a donation to the Win in the States Fund today.** ](https://act.swingleft.org/go/2629?t=5&akid=3094%2E1562180%2E3WeVz6)
With just 4 weeks left, we’re in a sprint to the finish—and we can’t thank you enough for everything you’re doing to help Democrats win in as many places as possible on November 3rd!
— The Swing Left Team

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** Right now, Swing Left is investing in grassroots organizing in key swing districts and initiatives across the country to flip the House and win the Senate and critical states in 2026. [**If you’d like to help support our work, you can make a donation using this link.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_sl_footer?refcode=em20261010-1&t=6&refcode2=3094_1562180_3WeVz6&akid=3094%2E1562180%2E3WeVz6)
